memory_update.text: FARM is the purest but riskiest restaurant/hospitality coffee and beverage DSD supplier candidate; keep as speculative_shadow until latest filings confirm liquidity, margin trajectory, DSD retention, and customer economics.
WEST is a cleaner small-cap underfollowed mapping to coffee, tea, flavors, extracts, private-label, RTD, foodservice, restaurant, convenience-store, and hospitality beverage solutions.

THS should be tracked as a mid-cap private-label beverage capacity owner after acquiring Farmer Brothers' Northlake coffee facility and direct-ship coffee business; restaurant exposure needs verification because the company may be more retail private-label than foodservice.

JVA is a micro-cap speculative exception with direct private-label, wholesale green coffee, foodservice, and coffee-equipment relevance; require strict survivability and customer-concentration diligence.

For this node, the likely chokepoints are not brand demand alone but green-coffee sourcing, roasting/extract capacity utilization, customer qualification, DSD/service execution, commodity pass-through, working capital, and leverage.
Need a follow-up pass on non-public but influential equipment/service vendors and syrup/extract formulators to identify any public parents or distributors with hidden exposure.

node: Private-label coffee, tea, extracts, syrups, and beverage solutions
summary: Layer 1B expands the restaurant beverage-input node into a focused universe of US-listed suppliers with direct or second-order exposure to private-label coffee, tea, extracts, syrups, foodservice beverage programs, direct-store-delivery, roasting/extract capacity, and customer qualification. The most relevant underfollowed names are Farmer Brothers, Westrock Coffee, TreeHouse Foods, and Coffee Holding Co. The bottleneck thesis is operational rather than purely demand-driven: sourcing green coffee, roasting/extract capacity, DSD/service execution, customer retention, commodity pass-through, leverage, and working-capital durability.
